newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Clarke in slip over election.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Clarke in slip over election.

text.p: British Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke produced an unfortunate slip of the tongue on Thursday that suggested he expected his Conservative Party to lose the forthcoming general election.
The Times newspaper published an interview with Clarke in which it said he began talking about "when" the opposition Labour Party got into power before hastily correcting himself to "if they get in".

Clarke was embroiled in a cabinet row on Wednesday after he said Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind had made "a slip of the tongue" in saying Britain was hostile to European Monetary Union (EMU). Rifkind said he had made no mistake.
On Thursday, the two ministers issued a joint statement denying any rift in government policy on EMU.

Prime Minister John Major insists he has every chance of winning the general election, which must be held by May, even though Labour has led by around 20 points in opinion polls for the last two years.
